lede: The biggest thing on the civic calendar this week is the San Miguel County BOCC meeting on August 5, where three Land Use Code amendments go to formal public hearing — including changes to who qualifies as an 'owner' under affordable housing rules, a wildfire areas update, and a continued hearing on nonconforming lots. The same day, the Open Space Commission takes up trail alignment for Reach 1 of the Valley Floor River Trail, with three routes around wetlands still in play. Ouray County's planning commission is also meeting virtually to work through definition changes in their land use code — the kind of quiet rewrite that shapes everything downstream.

notable.stake: Commissioners choose one of three Valley Floor River Trail alignments near wetlands.
Public hearings on three Land Use Code changes, including affordable housing ownership rules.
Definition rewrites in Ouray County's land use code can quietly shift what rules allow.
